name_reason: Name is accurate and free of address residue. 'byte_d' refers to combat_aux_block field index 0xD (a struct field offset documented in types.h as ai_class), 'low4' = the low 4 bits actually written, 'for_char_range' = the inclusive [start,end] loop. domain prefix fd2_ present. The literal offset-based descriptor matches how every caller comment in the codebase refers to this field (combat_aux_block[0xD]); a semantic rename to ai_class would be slightly clearer but the field is multi-purpose (AI mode / dialog control state per plate) so the literal name is safer and consistent. No param_1-style generic, no mismatch with body.
purpose: Set the low nibble (AI class / AI-dialog control flag) of combat_aux_block[0xD] for every runtime char in an inclusive index range, preserving the high nibble.
logic_summary: for (i = start_idx; (int)i <= (int)end_idx; i++) { pChar = runtime_char_array + i*RUNTIME_CHAR_SIZE; pChar[0x34] = (pChar[0x34] & 0xF0) | (uint8)new_val; }. pChar[0x34] == combat_aux_block[0xD] (combat_aux_block base = +0x27). The high 4 bits are preserved; new_val is OR'd raw (not pre-masked), so callers must pass 0..0xF for low-nibble-only semantics (all 15 callers do: values seen are 0, 3, 7). Signed comparison on the loop bound. Watcom __CHK(0xC) stack probe in prologue.
signature: void __cdecl fd2_set_combat_aux_block_byte_d_low4_for_char_range(uint32 start_idx, uint32 end_idx, uint32 new_val)

params.name: start_idx
params.semantics: First runtime_char_array index in the inclusive range to update (NPC/enemy group start). Compared signed against end_idx.
params.reason: Descriptive, matches body usage as the loop start index; no address residue.

params.name: end_idx
params.semantics: Last runtime_char_array index in the inclusive range (loop runs while i <= end_idx).
params.reason: Descriptive, matches the inclusive loop bound; no address residue.

params.name: new_val
params.semantics: New AI class / AI-dialog control flag value; only its low 4 bits are written into combat_aux_block[0xD]. Callers pass 0..0xF (0/3/7 observed).
params.reason: Accurately names the value being written; no address residue. (Body casts to (uint8) and ORs raw, hence the caller-must-mask note in the comment.)

returns.semantics: No return value; mutates runtime_char_array in place.

comment_original_issue: Original src comment was correct but terse: it stated only 'write low 4 bits of new_val into combat_aux_block[0xD] for chars in range' without noting the high-nibble preservation, the absolute offset 0x34, the field meaning (AI class / control flag), or the important caller-must-mask-to-0..0xF correctness note (body ORs raw, does not pre-mask).
notes: Validated semantics against types.h (combat_aux_block base +0x27, [0xD]=ai_class -> absolute 0x34) and against two callers (handler_3b passes (0x27,0x2C,0) to disarm; handler_30 passes (0x23,0x2A,3) and (0x43,0x4A,3) to arm AI mode 3). Many sibling caller comments in the codebase already reference combat_aux_block[0xD] by this literal offset, so keeping the name preserves cross-reference consistency. Ghidra plate is more verbose than src but consistent (documents same masking note, abs offset 0x34, 15 callers, AI/dialog control flag) -> left unchanged. No logic touched.
